why: Checks 1, 2, 3 and 5 test only what their expect lines say: exit 1 with empty stdout; `bad config:` plus the exact path plus line 3 column 3; `OK` vs `RETURNED`/`NO PATH`; head passes and a path-asserting test fails on the base src. Check 4 breaks the criterion. Its expect line only says the run "prints `listening on 9000` on stdout", exits 0 and returns { port: 9000 }. But its PASS needs "stdout is `listening on 9000`, then `exit 0`, then {\"port\":9000}" and its FAIL triggers on "any difference in output". That is an exact-output rule the words don't force: a PR that prints `listening on 9000` plus one extra stdout line meets the expect line but fails the check. It should be under Advisory.
